source.title: A limbic circuitry involved in emotional stress-induced grooming

confidence_rationale: Establishes that a non-feeding behaviour (self-grooming) is a homeostatically-regulated, positively-valenced de-arousal response with a dedicated limbic circuit (vSub -> LSv -> LH), not a deficit-reduction consummatory act. This grounds SD-060's core premise that needs beyond hunger/thirst (here: a de-arousal/comfort need) are first-class behavioural-homeostatic systems. Held at 0.62 because it evidences ONE non-feeding behaviour as homeostatically regulated (evidence-by-instance), not the full register, and grooming-as-displacement is a narrower category than the exploration/play/social axes SD-060 also enumerates.
failure_signatures: The paper evidences grooming specifically as a stress-induced de-arousal behaviour; it does not show that exploration, play, social contact, or learning are each independently homeostatically integrated, so generalising from grooming to the whole SD-060 register is an inductive leap this single circuit does not license.

The circuit is engaged by emotional stress (an aversive trigger); SD-060 also posits appetitive non-terminal drives (curiosity, play) whose regulation may follow a different, non-de-arousal logic -- so the homeostatic framing demonstrated here may not transfer to the appetitive axes.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Self-grooming is a frequently observed repetitive displacement behaviour believed to contribute to post-stress de-arousal with adaptive value, important in maintaining behavioural homeostasis. A di-synaptic limbic circuit (ventral subiculum -> ventral lateral septum -> lateral hypothalamus tuberal nucleus) regulates emotional-stress-induced self-grooming with positive affective valence; LSv activity peaks before grooming onset and inhibiting the circuit suppresses stress-triggered grooming.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-060 proposes a register of non-terminal drives -- exploration, play, social, learning, grooming, rest -- each carried as its own homeostatic-style integrator rather than collapsed into the SD-012 energy scalar. Mu et al. provide a concrete, mechanistically-anchored instance of one such axis: grooming is regulated to maintain BEHAVIOURAL homeostasis (de-arousal back to set-point) with positive valence and a dedicated circuit, exactly the homeostatic-style integrator SD-060 wants for non-feeding needs. It supports the project rule (feedback_biology_before_formal_definitions / L-non-terminal-needs) that non-feeding drives are homeostatically-regulated systems, not mere deficit-reduction -- here the regulated variable is arousal/affective state, not a consumed resource.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This grounds the homeostatic-regulation framing for ONE non-feeding behaviour (grooming-as-de-arousal under stress); it does not evidence the other SD-060 axes (exploration, play, social, learning) or show they share the same integrator architecture. Grooming here is triggered by an aversive emotional stressor, so it speaks to a de-arousal/comfort need rather than the appetitive non-terminal drives, which may be regulated differently. Rodent limbic circuit; transfer to REE assumes the behavioural-homeostasis principle (regulate a behavioural/affective variable to a set-point) is substrate-general.
mapping.source_context: In vivo rat study: optogenetic + fibre-photometry dissection of a ventral-subiculum -> ventral-lateral-septum -> lateral-hypothalamus circuit driving emotional-stress-induced self-grooming.

confidence_components.notes: Nat Commun, optogenetics + photometry circuit dissection (high source quality). Mapping_fidelity moderate: strong for the 'non-feeding behaviour IS homeostatically regulated' premise of SD-060, weak as evidence for the full multi-axis register; transfer_risk moderate (rodent stress-grooming -> general non-terminal-drive register).
